long_biography.plain_text:
Podiatric surgeon Stanley Kalish developed the TLS drain to remove fluid from surgical wounds. Its catheter connects to a vacuum tube that collects the drainage, adapting closed suction to foot surgery. The device entered commercial distribution, and he later co-authored a technical account of its use with Marla LaVoie.

At Roosevelt Warm Springs, he helped create a training link with Our Lady of Mercy Medical Center in New York. His professional relationships brought its podiatric residents into a permanent rotation in rehabilitation and reconstructive foot surgery. Local colleague Bhavin Mehta supervised the visiting residents, while Kalish served as the centre's medical director.
